name: 540° Stall Turn
description:
The **540° stall turn** replaces the standard half-rotation with a **1.5 full yaw rotation** (540°) at the top. The helicopter still ends pointing straight down, but the extended pirouette demands better rudder authority, heading control, and collective management during the spin.

### Execution Steps
1. Enter exactly as a standard stall turn — level flight → vertical climb.
2. At near-zero airspeed, apply **full rudder** and hold it through **one and a half complete rotations** (540°).
3. Count the rotations visually — the nose passes through "down" once (at 180°), back through "up" (at 360°), and finally settles on "down" again (540°).
4. Neutralise rudder precisely as the nose points straight down, then fly the vertical downline and pull out.

### Common Problems
- **Running Out of Energy:** The extended rotation takes longer, during which the helicopter sinks. Enter with slightly more speed to buy extra hang time at the top.
- **Inconsistent Rotation Rate:** The yaw rate may speed up or slow down as the helicopter drifts through different wind angles. Anticipate this and modulate rudder pressure to keep the pirouette smooth.
- **Stopping on the Wrong Heading:** Overshooting or undershooting the 540° mark is the most common error. Practice by counting the 180° waypoints (1 — nose down, 2 — nose up, 3 — nose down = stop) rather than trying to track degrees.
